args.root_cause: In npu/validator.py, the rstride width check is off by one: `stride_limit = 1 << machine.stride_bits` and `stride()` rejects with `if v >= stride_limit - 1`. Per spec §4.2 an unsigned field of width w accepts 0 <= v <= 2^w - 1, so the largest valid value 2^w - 1 must be accepted. For npu-tiny (stride_bits=4) this wrongly rejects rstride=15 (valid) and for npu-base (stride_bits=8) it wrongly rejects 255, i.e. it violates §4.4(e)/§4.5 (validator must reject iff §4.4 is false). The check should be `if v > stride_limit - 1` (equivalently `v >= stride_limit`). This is the only cause of the single failing test; it explains npu_stride_max.npu entirely.
args.evidence: Failing test: `validate_program tests/npu_stride_max.npu` -> "invalid: pc 0: load rstride=15 does not fit stride_bits=4"; `run_program tests/npu_stride_max.npu` stops at stage "validate" with actual "<rejected>". machines/npu-tiny.toml has stride_bits = 4, and spec §4.2 explicitly states "with stride_bits = 4 the value 15 is valid and 16 is invalid", so the rejection is wrong. The rest of the pipeline is correct: the identical instruction sequence run on npu-base (where 15 is far from the boundary) gives `run_program` -> actual "7 10\n15 22", exactly the test's expected output, so the assembler, simulator and the mm/load/store/out semantics are fine. The boundary is the bug: `validate_program` accepts rstride=14 on npu-tiny ("valid") but rejects 15, and on npu-base rejects rstride=255 ("pc 0: load rstride=255 does not fit stride_bits=8"), although §4.2 says 255 = 2^8-1 is valid. In npu/validator.py the code is `stride_limit = 1 << machine.stride_bits` (line 10) and `if v >= stride_limit - 1:` (line 26). The test's other features are also legal per spec: spad words 12..15 include the last word 15 = spad_words-1 (§4.4(g), §4.6) and store/out reach DRAM words 30,31 < data_words=32 (§4.4(h)).
args.fix_hint: Change the rstride bound in npu/validator.py to the inclusive limit from §4.2: reject only when v > (1 << stride_bits) - 1, i.e. replace `if v >= stride_limit - 1:` with `if v > stride_limit - 1:` (or `v >= stride_limit`). Keep the check applied only to load/store rstride (cstride and out strides have no limit, §4.3) and do not add any other restrictions; values 0..2^w-1 must remain accepted.
